name: classic-novels

description.en: 82 famous novels first published before 1950: the novels in Wikidata (works whose form or genre is novel) that the most Wikipedia language editions and other Wikimedia sites cover. Front: the novel's title in English and Swedish; back: its author. Compiled from Wikidata and LIBRIS, the National Library of Sweden's catalogue, and checked against Wikipedia. A few works whose authorship is traditional or uncertain, such as three of the four classic Chinese novels, are left out.
description.sv: 82 kända romaner som först gavs ut före 1950: de romaner i Wikidata (verk vars form eller genre är roman) som flest språkversioner av Wikipedia och andra Wikimediawebbplatser behandlar. Framsida: romanens titel på engelska och svenska; baksida: författaren. Sammanställd från Wikidata och Kungliga bibliotekets katalog LIBRIS och kontrollerad mot Wikipedia. Några verk vars författarskap är traditionellt tillskrivet eller osäkert, som tre av de fyra klassiska kinesiska romanerna, är inte med.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

Candidates came from Wikidata on 2026-10-04: every item that is an instance of literary work (Q7725634) whose form of creative work (P7937) is novel (Q8261) or whose genre (P136) is novel or a subclass of novel, with at least 40 sitelinks and a publication date (P577). The query is listed under Queries as q1; it returned 218 items ranked by sitelinks (wikibase:sitelinks, the number of Wikimedia sites — mostly Wikipedia language editions — with a page on the item). A first attempt (q1a) that required P31 novel or P136 novel directly returned no rows; an inspection query (q0) showed that famous novels are typed as literary work with a specific novel genre, which is why the genre path is followed through subclasses; a second query (q2) confirmed that no further novels hide under other classes (written work, book, novel as class). The deck is therefore the novels as Wikidata classifies them: a work that Wikidata gives only other genres is not a candidate, however often it is called a novel. Query q5 (run in the first review loop (rounds 1–3)) lists the literary works with 48 or more sitelinks that q1 misses and whose English description says novel or novella: The Little Prince (151 sitelinks), The Adventures of Pinocchio (84) and Heidi (52), described as novels but given genres such as fairy tale or children's fiction; four novellas (The Metamorphosis, A Christmas Carol, The Time Machine, Notes from Underground); and two works without a date (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, The Golden Ass). The Tale of Genji (116 sitelinks, genre tsukuri monogatari, no P577) is also outside q1. These were not added: the selection follows Wikidata's classification rather than hand-picking among borderline works.

Novels first published before 1950 were kept: the earliest year among the item's P577 values had to be before 1950. Items that are not novels in the ordinary sense, or whose authorship is traditional or disputed, were excluded (see Selection). The deck takes every remaining novel with at least 48 sitelinks; the next novels have 47, so the cut falls between two values.

Wikidata's dates were checked for errors that would wrongly move a famous novel across the 1950 line, and, in the first review loop (rounds 1–3), for wrong first-publication years generally (every card's P577 compared with the English and Swedish Wikipedia leads). In Search of Lost Time (Q464928) has the single P577 value 2000, which is wrong: it was published 1913–1927 (Swedish Wikipedia; Wikidata's own items for its first and last parts have P577 1913 and 1927), and LIBRIS holds the Swedish translation from 1964–1982. It was added with its sitelinks (59) by hand. The Master and Margarita (Q188538) has P577 1928, the year Bulgakov began writing it; English Wikipedia says it was first published in 1966–1967, so it was excluded. Three cards have a wrong Wikidata year that does not affect the selection (all are before 1950 either way): The Mysterious Island (1888; serialised 1874–1875, book 1875), The Last of the Mohicans (1824; published 1826) and Dream of the Red Chamber (earliest 1792, the second Cheng–Gao edition; first printed 1791). These cards carry no P577 check. Query q4 listed novels with 45 or more sitelinks and no P577: the Odyssey, the Epic of Gilgamesh and the Book of Judith (not novels), Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (2007) and The Golden Ass (48 sitelinks). The Golden Ass was not added because it has no Swedish label in Wikidata and LIBRIS shows no settled Swedish title (Den gyllne åsnan 1960, Den gyllene åsnan 1985, Metamorfoser eller Den gyllene åsnan 2024).

Each card's front is the novel's English title and its Swedish title. Both are the item's Wikidata labels (en, sv), except: Frankenstein, whose English label is the full title 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus' — the card uses the short title, Wikidata's preferred title (P1476) 'Frankenstein', and gives the full title in a note; Journey to the Centre of the Earth, whose English label begins with 'A' — the card uses 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth', a Wikidata English alias and P1476 value (also the English Wikipedia article title), checked as an alias; and Dr Jekyll och Mr Hyde, whose Swedish label 'Dr. Jekyll och Mr. Hyde' has full stops that most LIBRIS records leave out — the card uses the Wikidata alias 'Dr Jekyll och Mr Hyde', the form that begins 40 of the 48 Swedish-language LIBRIS records by Stevenson matching the search (from 1921); 8 (1959–2014), like Swedish Wikipedia, write 'mr' in lower case.

Each Swedish title was looked up in LIBRIS, the union catalogue of the National Library of Sweden, with the xsearch API: query tit:"<Swedish title>" förf:<author surname>, keeping Swedish-language records whose title begins with the card's title (a plain string-prefix match, so genitive titles such as 'Robinson Crusoes …' are counted too) and whose creator contains the surname. The first run fetched only the first 200 hits of each search; in the first review loop (rounds 1–3) every search was re-run with full paging (start=1, 201, 401 …), which corrected the counts of six cards and the earliest record of two (Robinson Crusoe, Oliver Twist). Every card's Swedish title was found as the title of Swedish editions of the novel by that author; the evidence names the earliest record whose title is the card's title as such (followed by nothing, a subtitle or other words, not a genitive ending; for Robinson Crusoe the earliest prefix match, the genitive 'Robinson Crusoes …' of 1826, is named as well), and, where an older spelling of the same title exists (Švejk: 'Svejks' from 1930; Karamazov: 'Karamasov' from 1918), also the earliest record with that spelling. Two titles needed a hand search: the Hobbit (LIBRIS catalogues 'Bilbo : en hobbits äventyr', with the colon of cataloguing practice where Wikidata and Swedish Wikipedia write 'Bilbo – En hobbits äventyr') and Dream of the Red Chamber (the Swedish translation in LIBRIS, by Pär Bergman, 2005–2010, reissued 2017, is catalogued as five volumes titled Guldåldern … Stenåldern under the uniform title Hongloumeng; Swedish Wikipedia names them parts of Drömmar om röda gemak). Where a novel has two established Swedish titles (the Hobbit: 1962 and 2007 translations; Ulysses: Odysseus 1946 and Ulysses 2012; Buddenbrooks: Huset Buddenbrook 1904 and Buddenbrooks 2005), the card keeps the Wikidata label and names the other title in a note.

Each card's back is the author given by Wikidata's author property (P50); all 82 items have exactly one best-ranked P50 value (the value the builder's checks read). Only The Count of Monte Cristo (Q191838) has a second P50 statement: Auguste Maquet (Q766768), at normal rank below Alexandre Dumas (Q38337, preferred rank); the card's back gives Dumas and a note names Maquet as his collaborator. The name is the author's Wikidata English label, untagged because a personal name has no language — except where English and Swedish write the name differently: Russian names are transliterated differently (Leo Tolstoy / Lev Tolstoj, Fyodor Dostoevsky / Fjodor Dostojevskij, Alexander Pushkin / Aleksandr Pusjkin, Nikolai Gogol / Nikolaj Gogol, from the Wikidata en and sv labels; for Dostoevsky the English Wikipedia spelling, also a Wikidata alias, was preferred to the label 'Fyodor Dostoyevsky'), and Alexandre Dumas the elder is 'Alexandre Dumas d.ä.' in Swedish (Wikidata sv label). Those cards carry English and Swedish backs.

Authorship was cross-checked against the LIBRIS records (the creator of the Swedish edition) and against the lead section of each novel's Swedish and English Wikipedia article, fetched with the MediaWiki API (titles from the Wikidata sitelinks). A script checked that each lead contains the card's title and the author's surname; every lead did, except the Swedish lead of Drömmar om röda gemak, whose body names Cao Xueqin and was read in full. For three Swedish articles (Alice i Underlandet, Candide, Alice i Spegellandet) the extract begins with a disambiguation hatnote; the evidence quotes the first sentence after it. The English leads write 'Dostoevsky'; Wikidata's English label is 'Dostoyevsky' (both are standard transliterations).

Notes were written by the authoring agent in its own words, from content sources only (Wikidata, LIBRIS records of Swedish editions, and a public-domain primary text), with Wikipedia used to verify them: the other Swedish titles of the Hobbit, Ulysses and Buddenbrooks (LIBRIS; the Wikidata Swedish aliases where they exist); Frankenstein's full original title (Wikidata English label) and its Swedish form (Wikidata Swedish alias); Eugene Onegin as a novel in verse (Wikidata P136 verse novel); In Search of Lost Time's seven volumes, 1913–1927 (Wikidata P527 and the P577 of the first and last parts); Dumas père and his son (Wikidata aliases, P40, P106); Auguste Maquet as Dumas's collaborator on The Count of Monte Cristo (Wikidata's normal-rank P50 statement on Q191838; Swedish Wikipedia's lead names him too); other English titles of The Stranger and Demons (Wikidata aliases); and the first printing of Dream of the Red Chamber in 1791 by Cheng Weiyuan and Gao E, who added 40 chapters to the 80 then circulating and said they had collected and edited them (their 1791 prefaces, public domain, read in the Chinese Wikisource transcription; confirmed by English Wikipedia). The Dream of the Red Chamber note deliberately does not say who wrote the last 40 chapters: English Wikipedia reports that this is debated, and the deck's back gives Cao Xueqin, the author named by Wikidata (P50) and by every LIBRIS record of the Swedish translation, including its last volume.

Every card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder against live Wikidata (438 in all): the author (P50), the English and Swedish titles (labels or aliases; P1476 for Frankenstein), the first-publication year used for the selection (P577; not for In Search of Lost Time, The Mysterious Island, The Last of the Mohicans and Dream of the Red Chamber, whose Wikidata years are wrong), the author's English label (and Swedish label for the names written differently in Swedish), and the facts in the notes where Wikidata states them (aliases, labels, P136, P527, P577 of the parts, P40). The deck was built with authored_decks.py and validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts). Label checks read the item's labels and aliases in the given language and also accept the language-neutral 'mul' label, which Wikidata uses as the default for languages without their own label: Jane Eyre (Q182961) and Victor Hugo (Q535) have no 'en' label, and their English text on the cards is the 'mul' label. Likewise, six authors have no 'sv' label and their Swedish name is the 'mul' label, the same as the untagged back: Victor Hugo (Q535), Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (Q5879), Agatha Christie (Q35064), Arthur Conan Doyle (Q35610), Mark Twain (Q7245) and Voltaire (Q9068); their cards carry no Swedish author-label check. Property checks read best-ranked (truthy) values only.
selection: The deck holds 82 novels first published before 1950: the novels in Wikidata (literary works whose form or genre, followed through subclasses, is novel) with at least 48 Wikimedia sitelinks on 2026-10-04 and a first publication date (P577) before 1950, plus In Search of Lost Time, whose Wikidata date (2000) is wrong. The ranking covers only works that Wikidata classes as novels: works that Wikidata gives other genres are not candidates even when often called novels — known cases with enough sitelinks are The Little Prince, The Adventures of Pinocchio, Heidi and The Tale of Genji (which also has no date) — and were not added by hand. Excluded although they ranked high enough (48 or more sitelinks): Thus Spoke Zarathustra (80; a philosophical work, not usually counted as a novel); The Master and Margarita (79; first published 1966–1967, Wikidata's 1928 is when writing began); Journey to the West (79), Romance of the Three Kingdoms (73) and Water Margin (61) (attribution to a single author is traditional and uncertain, so the back would not have one safe answer). Six further works in the candidate pool fell below the cut-off and were therefore not selected; they would also have been excluded for these reasons: Orlando Furioso (44; an epic poem), Lazarillo de Tormes (42; anonymous), And Quiet Flows the Don (42; authorship has been disputed), La Celestina (41; a work in dialogue, authorship partly disputed), Emile, or On Education (40; a treatise) and Jin Ping Mei (40; pseudonymous author). Dream of the Red Chamber was kept: Cao Xueqin is the author that Wikidata and the library catalogues name; a note says that the novel was first printed in 1791 by Cheng Weiyuan and Gao E, who added the last 40 of its 120 chapters, without taking a side in the debate over who wrote them. Short novels and novellas that Wikidata classes as novels (Animal Farm, Candide, Heart of Darkness, Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde) were kept as Wikidata classes them. The Golden Ass (48 sitelinks, no P577) was left out for want of a settled Swedish title. Sitelink counts change over time; the ranking is a snapshot of 2026-10-04 and decides only which novels are in the deck.

licensing: The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content sources are all CC0 or public domain. Wikidata (CC0) gives the selection (sitelink ranking and publication dates), the English and Swedish titles (labels, aliases, P1476), the authors (P50) and their names (labels), and most facts in the notes. LIBRIS gives the Swedish titles and translation years in three notes (the Hobbit, Ulysses, Buddenbrooks); these come from records of editions published in Sweden, the scope of the Swedish national bibliography, which the National Library of Sweden releases under CC0, and are bibliographic facts. The 1791 prefaces of the first printed edition of Dream of the Red Chamber are public domain worldwide; only facts were taken from them, not the punctuation added by Wikisource. The English and Swedish Wikipedias (CC BY-SA 4.0) were consulted only to verify titles, authors, dates and the facts in the notes; nothing on the cards — no wording, no fact and no selection — is taken from them alone, so their licence puts no conditions on the deck. The notes are the authoring agent's own wording.

rounds.lens: Sources and machine checks: Wikidata checks, LIBRIS title search, Wikipedia lead search, the builder's dossier checks
rounds.summary: Every card was checked against three sources besides Wikidata: a LIBRIS record of a Swedish edition with the card's Swedish title by the card's author, and the Swedish and English Wikipedia leads (title and author's surname present). The builder ran 419 Wikidata checks at first (436 after the first review loop (rounds 1–3)) (author, titles, first-publication year, author names). Discrepancies between the sources and how they were resolved are listed below.

findings.issue: Wikidata P577 is 2000 (the only value), which kept the novel out of the pre-1950 query although it was published 1913–1927 (Swedish Wikipedia; LIBRIS has the Swedish translation from 1964–1982).
findings.resolution: Added by hand with its 59 sitelinks; no P577 check on this card; the discrepancy is recorded in its evidence.

findings.issue: Wikidata P577 1928 put The Master and Margarita in the pre-1950 list; English Wikipedia: written 1928–1940, first published 1966–1967.
findings.resolution: Excluded: first published after 1950.

findings.issue: The Golden Ass has 48 sitelinks but no P577, so the query could not select it; it has no Swedish label in Wikidata and LIBRIS shows three Swedish titles (1960, 1985, 2024).
findings.resolution: Left out; recorded under Selection.

findings.issue: Wikidata's English label is the full title 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus'.
findings.resolution: Front uses 'Frankenstein' (Wikidata P1476 'Frankenstein', checked); full title in a note.

findings.issue: Wikidata's English label is 'A Journey to the Centre of the Earth'; the English Wikipedia article is 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth' and names the 'A …' form as a variant translation title.
findings.resolution: Front uses 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth', a Wikidata English alias and P1476 value (also the English Wikipedia title); checked as an alias (check added in the first review loop (rounds 1–3)).

findings.issue: Wikidata's Swedish label 'Dr. Jekyll och Mr. Hyde' matches one LIBRIS record (1987); 48 Swedish records by Stevenson begin with the title (earliest 1921): 40 as 'Dr Jekyll och Mr Hyde', 8 as 'Dr Jekyll och mr Hyde' (counts as corrected in round 4).
findings.resolution: Front uses 'Dr Jekyll och Mr Hyde', a Wikidata sv alias (checked).

findings.issue: Dostoevsky's Wikidata English label is 'Fyodor Dostoyevsky'; English Wikipedia writes 'Fyodor Dostoevsky'. Applies to all five Dostoevsky cards.
findings.resolution: Back uses 'Fyodor Dostoevsky', checked as a Wikidata English alias; both spellings are standard.

findings.issue: LIBRIS's authority form is 'Gogol, Nikolai'; Wikidata's sv label and the Swedish Wikipedia article use 'Nikolaj Gogol'.
findings.resolution: Swedish back keeps 'Nikolaj Gogol' (Wikidata sv label, Swedish Wikipedia).

findings.issue: Two established Swedish titles: 'Bilbo – En hobbits äventyr' (1962 translation, catalogued 'Bilbo : en hobbits äventyr') and 'Hobbiten eller Bort och hem igen' (2007).
findings.resolution: Front keeps the Wikidata label; a note names the 2007 title.

findings.issue: Two established Swedish titles: 'Odysseus' (1946 translation, Wikidata label) and 'Ulysses' (2012 translation).
findings.resolution: Front keeps 'Odysseus'; a note names the 2012 title.

findings.issue: The Swedish translation is catalogued in LIBRIS as five volumes under the uniform title Hongloumeng, not as 'Drömmar om röda gemak'.
findings.resolution: Kept the Wikidata/Swedish Wikipedia title 'Drömmar om röda gemak' (Swedish Wikipedia names the volumes parts of it). (The note on the last 40 chapters was rewritten in the first review loop (rounds 1–3).)

findings.issue: Wikidata's Swedish labels write initials without spaces ('J.R.R. Tolkien', 'H.G. Wells'); the English labels have spaces.
findings.resolution: Personal names are untagged and use the English label's form, also used by LIBRIS ('Tolkien, J. R. R.', 'Wells, H. G.').

findings.resolution: No P577 check on this card; the discrepancy is recorded in its evidence. The selection is unaffected (before 1950 either way).

rounds.scope: All 82 cards: authors, titles, notes, selection query q1 re-run, P50 and P577 of every item, LIBRIS searches for alternative Swedish titles
rounds.summary: All 82 authors and every front were found correct and unambiguous. The reviewer found one error (the Dream of the Red Chamber note stated a disputed attribution of the last 40 chapters to Gao E as the usual view), three P577 checks asserting wrong first-publication years, a selection description that overstated what the genre-based query covers, a second current Swedish title for Buddenbrooks, and two documentation slips.
